Quick triage notes: I pulled the traced request IDs Rachel sent and matched them to ingress logs and our trace sampling. Observations:

- Temporal correlation: most customer errors line up with 2026-10-07 09:40-11:15 PDT window.
- Server metrics: small uptick in CPU on a subset of pods, but not a cluster-wide saturation.
- Connection pattern: a large fraction of requests from BrightWare are short-lived TCP connections with a high retry rate; we also saw many repeated request IDs within seconds (suggesting client retries re-sent identical payloads).
- Latency distribution: tail moved up, but median unchanged — classic amplification.

My hypothesis: an increase in client-side timeouts (either from BrightWare or their CDN) led to immediate retries from their SDK which increased instantaneous load and pushed some backend hosts into transient queueing—this inflated p95/p99. There are also a small number of true 5xx root causes (upstream infra timeouts) we need Dylan to confirm.

I added a Grafana snapshot to the thread: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/hosting/hosted-api-latency?orgId=1

—Sean

Subject: Re: Slowdowns + 5xx bursts on Hosted API - urgent

Digging into infra traces and request traces now. Preliminary findings: 

1) There are two distinct contributors: a) ~0.6% of the spikes are server-side upstream timeouts (we have open follow-ups on a dependency that had a GC pause) and b) the majority looks like a feedback/retry amplification.

2) SDK behavior: We've identified that an older Redwood SDK (common in customer fleets) defaults to short socket timeouts with an immediate fixed retry (no jitter/exponential backoff) for idempotent requests when it sees a reset. There's a behavior in node-sdk v1.4.2 where connection resets trigger 3 rapid retries within ~200ms. That will absolutely create bursts under load.

3) Traffic fingerprinting: BrightWare's requests clustered by client-ip, and replay density is high — the same payloads repeated many times during the window.

Suggested mitigations (short term):
- Apply a soft server-side rate limiter for repeated identical request hashes (configurable threshold) for the next 24-48 hours to reduce amplification.
- Push an emergency patch to the SDK (v1.4.3) to add exponential backoff + jitter and increase default socket timeout. I'll prepare a patch and release notes.
- Ask BrightWare to temporarily raise their client timeout to 3s and disable fast retries.

I'll file INF-4928 for the SDK patch and coordinate a mitigation window.

—Dylan
SRE
